title: Iterated Integrals and Symmetry in Several Variables
quickIdea: A multiple integral is evaluated one variable at a time from the inside out, and over a box symmetric about the origin a term that is odd in one variable contributes nothing.
remember: Evaluate from the innermost differential outward, treating every other variable as a constant.
With constant limits the order of integration can be swapped without changing the value; with variable limits it cannot, because the limits then depend on the outer variable.
Odd symmetry extends term by term: over a box symmetric in y, any term odd in y integrates to zero; over a box symmetric in z, any term odd in z does so. The 2023 question dies twice over.
A term can be even in every variable and still vanish only if it is odd in at least one - check each term separately rather than the whole integrand at once.
The multi-variable odd rule is the single-variable rule applied one variable at a time; the joint condition f(-x, -y, -z) = -f(x, y, z) is sufficient but not necessary.
A quick size check: for a box, the integral of a constant k is k times the volume of the box.

example.prompt: Evaluate the integral from -3 to 3, from -2 to 2, from -1 to 1 of (4x^2 y - z^3) dz dy dx.
example.work: The inner integral in z: an antiderivative of 4x^2 y is 4x^2 y z, and of z^3 is z^4/4, so the inner value is 8x^2 y - 0 = 8x^2 y, because z^4/4 is the same at -1 and at 1. The middle integral in y of 8x^2 y from -2 to 2 is 0, since y is odd. The outer integral is then 0.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2023 Q.21 is this integral and the answer is 0. It is a numerical-answer question, so the only route to the marks is spotting the odd terms; computing it by hand costs time and invites an arithmetic slip. The exam has used the same trick in single-variable form in 2026 Set 2 Q.17.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2023 Q.21: the value of the integral from -3 to 3, from -2 to 2, from -1 to 1 of (4x^2 y - z^3) dz dy dx, rounded to the nearest integer, is ____.
variations.why: 4x^2 y is odd in y, so its integral over the symmetric y-range is 0, and z^3 is odd in z, so its integral over the symmetric z-range is 0. Every layer therefore contributes nothing and the value is exactly 0.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: What is the integral of xy over the unit square [0, 1] x [0, 1]?
variations.why: Here the limits are not symmetric, so no cancellation applies. Integrating in y first gives x/2, and then in x gives 1/4. The contrast with the 2023 question is the point: symmetry needs both the odd integrand and the symmetric range.

trap.what: Assuming a term vanishes because it contains a variable that appears to an odd power, without checking that the range for that variable is symmetric.
trap.why: The odd rule needs both conditions. On [0, 1] the integral of y is 1/2, not 0, and the same term that dies on [-2, 2] survives.
trap.counterexample: The integral of 4x^2 y over x in [0, 3], y in [0, 2], z in [0, 1] is 4 times (x^3/3 evaluated 0 to 3 = 9) times (y^2/2 evaluated 0 to 2 = 2) times 1 = 72, not 0. Only the symmetric box kills it.

check.question: Evaluate the integral from -1 to 1, from -1 to 1 of x^2 y dy dx.
check.explanation: The inner integral in y of x^2 y over the symmetric range is 0 because y is odd; x^2 does not matter. The outer integral of 0 is 0. If the y-range were [0, 1] the inner value would be x^2/2 and the answer 1/3.
